reasons: The finding correctly identifies the deviation: the grant is expressly 'non-transferable', limits affiliate use to Authorized Locations, and is silent on contractors, with Sections 3(c) and 20(d) blocking any successor transfer — squarely short of the preferred position.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it adds affiliates plus contractors/outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, strikes 'non-transferable' and adds an express successor-transfer right, and makes conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d) so the grant is not undercut elsewhere.

The changed-character ratios are high only because the grant and assignment sentences must be restructured to insert the licensee-side parties and the successor carve-out; no unrelated concessions or new obligations were introduced, so the advisory minimality flags are acceptable here.

Directionally correct for the customer and internally consistent: the Authorized Location limitation survives in clause (i) and the additional-fee sentence, so removing the trailing 'operating at Authorized Locations' phrase from the affiliate reference does not covertly expand geographic scope.

Comment is accurate and appropriately scoped — it concedes that the perpetual term in Section 17(a) already satisfies the no-at-will-revocation element, cites the playbook basis, and explains the conforming edits in one or two sentences in the required voice. Minor point to verify on turn: confirm the grant clause is in fact 'Section 2' as cross-referenced in the Section 3(c) carve-out.
